newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Unicom, Catch in mobile phone pact.
newsitem.headline: China's Unicom, Catch in mobile phone pact.

text.p: China Unicom and Beijing Catch Communications have signed an agreement to build a digital mobile telephone network in Beijing, the Economic Information Daily said on Wednesday.

The newspaper said that Unicom, or China United Telecommunications Corp, and Beijing Catch would cooperate in constructing a GSM (global system for mobile communications) network with an initial capacity of 100,000 subscribers in the second half of this year and doubling that figure by 1999.
Officials of the two companies were unable to give further details of the terms of the agreement.
China Unicom is a joint venture of 16 major Chinese organisations, led by the ministries of power, railways and electronics industry.
It was set up in 1994 to compete with the ministry of posts and telecommunications, which previously had a monopoly in providing telephone services.
Much of its business so far has been in mobile telephones.
Beijing Catch, a subsidiary of Shenzhen-listed Hainan Minyuan Modern Agricultural Development Co, conducts paging operations in the Chinese capital.
